chunks: He (peace be upon him) said to a man whom he saw striving against his enemy with what was harmful to himself too:
You are like one who pierces a spear through himself in order to kill the person sitting behind him.

key_terms.رِدْفَهُ: his back / the person behind him

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the metaphor about piercing oneself to kill the person behind?
ai.summary: In this concise metaphor from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) critiques the self-destructive nature of aggressive pursuit, comparing the man to a spearman who pierces his own back to strike the rider behind him. This imagery highlights the principle of 'self-harm in pursuit of harming others,' a concept deeply rooted in Shia ethical teachings regarding the balance between external action and internal preservation. The saying serves as a practical warning against sacrificing one's own well-being or spiritual integrity in the zeal to defeat an adversary.
